 Hon'Ble Krishan Pahal, J.
1 .  List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Raja Ram Pal, learned counsel for applicant, Sri Pranshu Kumar, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
3.

The present bail application has been filed by the applicant in Case Crime No.327 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B I.P.C. and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station-Alinagar, District-Chandauli with the prayer to enlarge him on bail.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the FIR is delayed by about five hours and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
The cause of death is Asphyxia as a result of ante-mortem hanging.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The trial is moving at snail's pace, as only two witnesses have been examined.
The applicant is in jail since 14.09.2022, as such, he is in incarceration for about three years.
Applicant is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
5. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that the FIR is prompt and cause of death is asphyxia as a result of ante-mortem injury.
The deceased has expired within the precincts of the house of the applicant, as such, he is not entitled for bail.
6. This Court had called for status of trial from the trial court concerned.

As per the status report dated 30.07.2025 received from the trial court concerned, two witnesses have been examined and non-bailable warrant has been issued against the co-accused person Pyare Lal Bind (father of applicant) since 01.02.2025.

7. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the status report which indicates that co-accused Pyare Lal Bind who is father of the applicant had absconded and the trial has been brought to a stand still, I do not find it a fit case for grant of bail to the applicant.
8. The bail application is found devoid of merits and is, accordingly, rejected.

9. However, it is directed that the aforesaid case pending before the trial court be decided expeditiously in view of the principle as has been laid down in the recent judgments of the Supreme Court in the cases of Vinod Kumar vs. State of Punjab; 2015 (3) SCC 220 and Hussain and Another vs. Union of India; (2017) 5 SCC 702, if there is no legal impediment.
